items.title: Burrill Crohn interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, January 3, 2012
items.q: I did a film on Joe Williams, a documentary on Joe Williams that Monk was very involved in

ctx.x: Well getting back to this, it’s almost step one, you get this idea and then you have to find some funding. Now you’ve got to research, right?

Well things have changed. Everything’s changing. Like technology is changing, information is changing, everything is changing. When I first started doing films, first of all budgets were bigger, because the price of entry was much more expensive. You are shooting on a camera that costs about three thousand dollars, if my memory serves me. I was shooting on cameras that cost seventy thousand dollars. Editing was three or four hundred dollars an hour, or you could edit off-line for fifty or seventy dollars an hour.…

something about jazz. It was a big contract. It was like a half a million dollar contract to do a ten episode series on the history of jazz. David Chertok had set that up actually. And I spent a week in Japan with an attorney, sitting at a conference table with the Japanese. That was funny in itself because they had a translator there, and they would say something in Japanese and then translate it, and then we’d talk among ourselves, and then come up with our answer.
